name: gpt-oss-120b
definition: gpt-oss-120b is a text reasoning Mixture-of-Experts model developed by OpenAI in the gpt-oss family. It has 116.8B parameters with 5.1B/token active parameters, supports 131,072 tokens of context, accepts Text and produces Text. Its primary role is reasoning, tool-oriented workflows and high-capability self-hosted inference.

key_topics: reasoning, tool-oriented workflows and high-capability self-hosted inference

details: 128 experts with 4 experts active per token
Alternating dense and locally banded sparse attention
Grouped multi-query attention with group size 8
MXFP4 quantized checkpoint designed for efficient memory use

training.summary: OpenAI describes pretraining on a mostly English, text-only corpus with emphasis on STEM, coding and general knowledge, followed by supervised fine-tuning and high-compute reinforcement learning. The model uses the Harmony response format and exposes configurable reasoning effort.

license.name: Apache License 2.0
license.special_conditions: Includes an express patent grant. Model-specific acceptable-use policies, if separately published, are not automatically part of Apache 2.0.
license.legal_note: OpenWeightModels summary for technical comparison; not legal advice.

deployments.notes: Official Hugging Face integration for direct inference and experimentation.
Documented production serving path with OpenAI-compatible endpoints.
OpenAI documents local deployment paths for gpt-oss; the 120B model remains a high-memory workload.

hardware.summary: OpenAI states that the 120B checkpoint was designed to fit on a single 80 GB accelerator. That statement refers to model weights under the released quantization; KV cache, batch size, long context and runtime buffers still consume additional memory.

limitations: Text-only model; it does not natively accept images or audio.
The 128K context increases KV-cache pressure and can materially change memory requirements.
A permissive software license does not remove the need to follow OpenAI’s separate usage policy and applicable law.
Self-hosting shifts safety controls, monitoring and operational reliability to the deployer.
